Harbour Notes

How the tide tables are made

Tide tables combine decades of water level readings with the positions of the moon and the sun. Each harbour has its own constants, which is why two ports a few miles apart can differ by an hour.

Why old harbours silt up

Rivers carry sand and mud to the sea, and slow water drops what it carries. Without regular dredging a harbour mouth becomes shallow within a few decades.
